leads.summary: Fixed layout-reset timeout can exhaust a short suspend inhibitor budget before the first lock retry
leads.consequence: With logind configured for a 2-second InhibitDelayMaxUSec, this script derives a 1000ms budget. If the initial lock request is lost and both Hyprland layout IPC and clamshell reconciliation stall, the new 400ms timeout plus the existing 400ms timeout leaves too little for the status poll and retry. The script returns 1 and emits 'Screen did not lock before suspend', releasing its delay inhibitor without a confirmed secure lock. A suspend waiting on that inhibitor is no longer held back by this helper. The same isolated scenario against the merge-base (which is identical to the current quattro tip for this script) retries and obtains a secure lock. The shipped default 5s/15s windows give more slack; this is conditional on a short custom logind window and two simultaneous stalls. Suggested change: clip the best-effort calls to remaining budget and reserve enough time for at least one status poll and lock retry, or perform the optional layout reset only when doing so preserves that retry window.
leads.triage: sent to Opus (followup-1); confirmed only in narrow admin-lowered logind windows (~1.5-1.9 s, ~2.5-2.9 s) with Hyprland IPC stall; identical to base at 2/3/5/15 s; not published (below systemd 5 s default, shipped 15 s); behavioural

leads.summary: Sleep-lock tests still call real Hyprland and do not test the newly introduced layout reset
leads.consequence: The existing fixture stubs omarchy-shell, busctl, clamshell and notifications, but never hyprctl; all seven scenarios invoke switchxkblayout all 0 on the runner's actual Hyprland when the developer runs test/shell in a session. A fake hyprctl PATH interceptor recorded seven layout switches while every fixture assertion passed. Omitting the reset or changing its argument to all 1 would likewise not be detected. Suggested change: add a hyprctl stub to setup_scenario, assert its ordering/arguments and that timeout lets the lock continue when the stub hangs; adjust calls[] ordering as appropriate. Related open PR #13480 adds a stub in its own modified test; it merged without conflict with this PR in an isolated fixture run but has not landed on this pinned head.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F2); corroborated; factual

# F2: sleep-lock-test.sh calls the real hyprctl and never asserts the layout reset

Reviewed head: `fb9f4a7e8c12c973ee510b61a5972451cb936129`. Earlier head: `3f745c0e8f6feda0bb9ddae95e113dec5ff3b60e`. Merge-base: `d201fb9564777fe5a8c587b4ef93a48106720f2e`.

All commands run from the repository root of a checkout of the named commit. A recording `hyprctl` placed first on `PATH` stands in for the one a developer has inside a Hyprland session. Outputs below are unedited, captured in an isolated sandbox with no Hyprland session.

## A. The unchanged test calls whatever `hyprctl` is on PATH

```bash
fake=$(mktemp -d)
printf '#!/bin/bash\nprintf "%%s\\n" "$*" >>"%s/calls"\n' "$fake" >"$fake/hyprctl"
chmod +x "$fake/hyprctl"
: >"$fake/calls"
PATH="$fake:$PATH" bash test/shell.d/sleep-lock-test.sh >/dev/null 2>&1
echo "test exit: $?"
echo "hyprctl calls: $(wc -l <"$fake/calls")"
sort "$fake/calls" | uniq -c
```

Output at `fb9f4a7` (PR head):

```text
test exit: 0
hyprctl calls: 7
      7 switchxkblayout all 0
```

Output at `3f745c0`:

```text
test exit: 0
hyprctl calls: 7
      7 switchxkblayout all 0
```

Output at `d201fb9` (merge-base, no reset in the script):

```text
test exit: 0
hyprctl calls: 0
```

The 7 calls come from the 7 scenarios that reach the reset (the `missing_pam` scenario exits before it). With the real `hyprctl` inside a Hyprland session, each call would set every keyboard of the developer running the suite to its first layout (from Hyprland's `switchxkblayout all` handler; not observed in a live session).

## B. Proposed test: stub `hyprctl` per scenario, assert the reset, bound a stalled reset

```diff
--- a/test/shell.d/sleep-lock-test.sh
+++ b/test/shell.d/sleep-lock-test.sh
@@ -17,14 +17,20 @@
   state_dir="$scenario_dir/state"
   notify_log="$scenario_dir/notifications"
   journal_log="$scenario_dir/journal"
+  hyprctl_log="$scenario_dir/hyprctl"
   mkdir -p "$mock_bin" "$state_dir"
   : >"$notify_log"
   : >"$journal_log"
+  : >"$hyprctl_log"
 
   # The budget is derived from logind, so pin the window rather than letting the
   # host's own configuration decide what these scenarios are testing.
   mock_logind_window 5000000
 
+  # Keep the layout reset away from the compositor of whoever runs the suite,
+  # and record it so the scenarios can assert it.
+  mock_hyprctl
+
   # Capture the desktop warning instead of firing a real one at whoever is
   # running the suite.
   cat >"$mock_bin/omarchy-notification-send" <<SH
@@ -44,6 +50,16 @@
   chmod +x "$mock_bin/busctl"
 }
 
+mock_hyprctl() {
+  cat >"$mock_bin/hyprctl" <<SH
+#!/bin/bash
+
+printf '%s\n' "\$*" >>"$hyprctl_log"
+sleep ${1:-0}
+SH
+  chmod +x "$mock_bin/hyprctl"
+}
+
 mock_clamshell() {
   cat >"$mock_bin/omarchy-hyprland-monitor-clamshell" <<SH
 #!/bin/bash
@@ -103,6 +119,35 @@
   fail "sleep lock bounds a stalled clamshell sync" "elapsed: ${elapsed_us}us"
 pass "sleep lock bounds a stalled clamshell sync"
 
+[[ $(< "$hyprctl_log") == "switchxkblayout all 0" ]] ||
+  fail "sleep lock resets the keyboard layout to the first layout" \
+    "hyprctl calls: $(< "$hyprctl_log")"
+pass "sleep lock resets the keyboard layout to the first layout"
+
+# hyprctl only gives up on a stalled Hyprland after its own 5s socket timeout,
+# so the layout reset must be bounded like the clamshell sync.
+setup_scenario stalled_layout_reset
+cat >"$mock_bin/omarchy-shell" <<'SH'
+#!/bin/bash
+
+printf 'shell %s\n' "$*" >>"$CALL_LOG"
+if [[ $* == "lock lock" ]]; then
+  printf 'ok\n'
+elif [[ $* == "lock status" ]]; then
+  printf '{"secure":true}\n'
+fi
+SH
+chmod +x "$mock_bin/omarchy-shell"
+mock_clamshell
+mock_hyprctl 10
+
+run_sleep_lock 4000
+
+(( exit_status == 0 && elapsed_us < 1500000 )) ||
+  fail "sleep lock bounds a stalled layout reset" \
+    "exit: $exit_status elapsed: ${elapsed_us}us"
+pass "sleep lock bounds a stalled layout reset"
+
 # A shell that never secures the session must give up inside the budget rather
 # than hold logind's delay inhibitor open.
 setup_scenario never_secure
```

```bash

before=$(wc -l <"$fake/calls")
PATH="$fake:$PATH" bash test/shell.d/sleep-lock-test.sh 2>&1
echo "test exit: $?"
echo "hyprctl calls reaching PATH during the proposed test: $(( $(wc -l <"$fake/calls") - before ))"
```

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified** (sandbox runs of the script with the real `hyprctl` against a fake Hyprland socket, stubbed shell and clamshell helpers):

- Line 117 is exactly the suggested bounded call, still after `request_lock` and before `sync_clamshell`.
- Stalled socket (clamshell helper not stalled): `fb9f4a7` exits 0 in 0.465 s with a 15 s or 5 s window, against 5.3 to 5.4 s at `3f745c0`; with a lost first lock request it re-requests and locks in 0.565 s. With the clamshell helper also stalled, `fb9f4a7` takes 0.82 to 0.97 s.
- Healthy socket: the reset is served in about 10 ms. A socket that accepts 2 s late still receives it after `hyprctl` is killed, and Hyprland's IPC handler (source) runs the command before replying.
- `sleep-lock`, `sleep-monitor`, `system-lock`, `keyboard-layout` and `hyprland-keyboard-layout` shell tests pass at `fb9f4a7`.
- The new comment matches `default/hypr/input.lua`, which makes the first layout Latin by default.

#13156 (head `58b11fe`) is also unchanged: a redundant but harmless reset from the lock service. #13640 and #13480 add a default `hyprctl` stub to the same test, which would remove the side effect but not assert the reset; both merge cleanly with this PR.
</details>
